k: A mutant master of magnetism who distrusts humanity
st: Magneto kidnaps Senator Kelly and tests a machine that forces humans to mutate.
He aims the machine at world leaders on Ellis Island, but the X-Men stop him and he lands in a plastic prison.
Freed by Mystique, he joins the X-Men against Stryker, then turns Cerebro against humanity.
He builds a new Brotherhood, recruits the Phoenix, and attacks Alcatraz to destroy the mutant cure.
Beast injects him with the cure, but alone in a park he makes a metal chess piece move.
In a dark future, he fights the Sentinels side by side with Charles Xavier.

k: A shape-shifting mutant who serves Magneto
st: Mystique poses as Bobby Drake to sabotage Cerebro, then fights the X-Men at the Statue of Liberty.
Wolverine stabs her, but she survives and takes Senator Kelly's place in public.
She breaks Magneto out of his plastic prison and helps the X-Men raid Stryker's base.
Freed from a prison convoy, she takes a cure dart meant for Magneto and loses her powers.
Abandoned by Magneto, she tells the government where to find him.

k: A feral mutant enforcer in Magneto's Brotherhood
st: Sabretooth ambushes Wolverine and Rogue on a snowy road, then captures Rogue for Magneto.
Cyclops blasts him out of the Statue of Liberty's head, and he falls far below.
In the Void, a Sabretooth variant takes on Wolverine, and Wolverine cuts off his head.

k: A leaping, long-tongued mutant in the Brotherhood
st: Toad fights the X-Men at the train station and inside the Statue of Liberty.
Storm strikes him with lightning, and he falls into the water.
A Toad variant fights for Cassandra Nova in the Void, and Blade kills him in the raid on her lair.

k: John Allerdyce, a hot-headed student who controls fire
st: John Allerdyce sets police cars ablaze, then leaves the X-Men to join Magneto at Alkali Lake.
As Pyro, he joins the Brotherhood's attack on Alcatraz, and Iceman beats him in a duel.
In the Void, he serves Cassandra Nova while secretly working for Paradox of the TVA.
Cassandra Nova learns of his betrayal and kills him.

k: A U.S. Army officer running secret mutant programs
st: Stryker leads Team X, a covert unit of mutant soldiers, on brutal missions.
He bonds adamantium to Logan's skeleton in the Weapon X program, then orders his memory wiped.
He unleashes Weapon XI, then shoots Logan in the head with adamantium bullets, erasing his memory.
Military police arrest him for the murder of General Munson.
Stryker raids the X-Mansion and uses his son's power to turn Cerebro against every mutant.
Wolverine leaves him chained at Alkali Lake, and he dies when the dam bursts.

k: Yuriko, Stryker's mind-controlled mutant bodyguard
st: Under Stryker's control, Yuriko serves as his silent enforcer at Alkali Lake.
Wolverine floods her body with liquid adamantium, and she dies.
A Lady Deathstrike variant stands among Cassandra Nova's forces in the Void.

k: Stryker's son, a mutant who casts illusions
st: Stryker uses Jason's illusions to control Charles Xavier through a copy of Cerebro.
Storm and Nightcrawler free Xavier, and Jason is left behind as the base floods.

k: A senator pushing the Mutant Registration Act
st: Senator Kelly argues that mutants are dangerous and must be registered.
Magneto's machine mutates him, and he dies as his body turns to water.

k: Jean Grey's unleashed, all-powerful dark side
st: Jean returns from Alkali Lake as the Phoenix and destroys Charles Xavier.
She sides with Magneto and tears Alcatraz apart in a rage.
Wolverine kills her to stop the destruction.

k: An unstoppable mutant held in a prison convoy
st: Magneto frees Juggernaut from a prison convoy, and he joins the Brotherhood.
At Alcatraz he hunts the boy Leech, but Kitty Pryde tricks him into charging headfirst into a wall.

k: A super-fast mutant who can sense other mutants
st: Callisto helps Magneto find mutants and joins his Brotherhood.
Storm kills her in the battle at Alcatraz.

k: A mutant thief who can copy himself
st: Magneto frees Multiple Man from a prison convoy and recruits him.
His copies act as a decoy at the Brotherhood's camp, and soldiers take him in.

k: Logan's savage brother, a mutant soldier
st: Victor fights beside his brother Logan through a century of wars, then joins Stryker's Team X.
He hunts down Team X's former members for Stryker and appears to kill Kayla Silverfox.
Victor helps Logan defeat Weapon XI, then walks away.

k: Stryker's ultimate weapon, built from Wade Wilson
st: Stryker turns Wade Wilson, a Team X mercenary, into Weapon XI, loaded with stolen mutant powers.
Logan and Victor defeat him, and Logan cuts off his head.
After the credits, his severed head opens its eyes.

k: Team X's deadly sharpshooter
st: Agent Zero hunts Logan for Stryker and kills the elderly couple who take him in.
Logan downs his helicopter and kills him in the explosion.

k: A venomous mutant doctor serving the Yashida family
st: Posing as Yashida's doctor, Viper plants a parasite in Logan that stops him from healing.
Yukio kills her in the final battle at Yashida's research facility.

k: A dying billionaire Logan saved at Nagasaki
st: Yashida, the soldier Logan saved at Nagasaki, offers to take away Logan's healing power.
He fakes his death and, inside the Silver Samurai armor, starts draining Logan's healing factor.
Mariko stabs him with Logan's claws, and Logan throws him from the tower.

k: Mariko's father and heir to the Yashida empire
st: Shingen sends Yakuza to kidnap his own daughter at her grandfather's funeral.
He duels Logan with a sword and dies on his claws.

k: A ninja archer sworn to protect Mariko
st: Harada's ninjas capture Logan for Yashida's plan.
He turns on Yashida to protect Mariko, and the Silver Samurai kills him.

k: A Nazi scientist who absorbs energy
st: As Klaus Schmidt, a Nazi doctor, he kills young Erik's mother to unlock the boy's powers.
Leading the Hellfire Club, he pushes the U.S. and the USSR toward nuclear war over Cuba.
Erik pins him inside his submarine and drives the old coin through his skull.

k: A Hellfire Club telepath who turns to diamond
st: Emma Frost bends a Soviet general's mind to serve Shaw's plan.
Erik captures her in Russia, and the CIA locks her up.
Erik breaks her out, and she joins his Brotherhood.

k: A red-skinned teleporter in the Hellfire Club
st: Azazel teleports into the CIA's base with Shaw and kills the agents there.
After Shaw dies, he joins Erik's Brotherhood.
An Azazel variant serves Cassandra Nova in the Void.

k: A Hellfire Club mutant who spins up whirlwinds
st: Riptide fights for Shaw at the CIA base and in the battle off Cuba.
After Shaw dies, he joins Erik's Brotherhood.

k: A winged mutant recruited by the CIA
st: Angel abandons the young mutants and joins Shaw after his attack on the CIA base.
After Shaw dies, she joins Erik's Brotherhood.

k: Erik Lehnsherr, a Holocaust survivor hunting Nazis
st: Erik hunts the Nazi who killed his mother and teams up with Charles Xavier.
He kills Shaw, turns the navies' missiles back on them, and leaves with Mystique as Magneto.
Freed from a Pentagon cell in 1973, he hijacks Sentinels and attacks the White House.
After his family is killed, he becomes a Horseman of Apocalypse and tears at the Earth's metal.
He turns on Apocalypse, then helps rebuild Xavier's school.
Living on Genosha, he hunts Jean for killing Mystique, then fights beside her against the D'Bari.

k: Raven, a shape-shifter raised as Charles's sister
st: Raven embraces her blue form and leaves with Erik as Mystique.
In 1973 she hunts Bolivar Trask, whose experiments have killed mutants she knew.
She spares Trask, saves the President from Magneto, and walks away.
She rallies young mutants against Apocalypse and stays to train the X-Men.
An out-of-control Jean Grey throws her onto broken wood, and she dies.

k: A scientist building robots to hunt mutants
st: Trask experiments on captured mutants and sells his Sentinel program in 1973.
After Mystique spares him, he is arrested for selling military secrets.

k: Mutant-hunting robots that rule a dark future
st: In a dark future, Sentinels that copy mutant powers hunt mutants and the humans who help them.
In 1973, Magneto hijacks Trask's Sentinel prototypes and attacks the White House.
Mystique spares Trask, and Logan wakes in a future with no Sentinels.

k: A young Army major working with Bolivar Trask
st: Major William Stryker serves as Bolivar Trask's military aide in 1973.
Colonel Stryker raids Xavier's mansion and takes several X-Men to Alkali Lake.
Weapon X breaks loose, and his captives escape the base.

k: En Sabah Nur, the first mutant, worshipped as a god
st: Betrayed in ancient Egypt, En Sabah Nur is buried alive for thousands of years.
Woken in 1983, he gathers four Horsemen and seizes Charles Xavier's mind.
He sends the world's nuclear missiles into space and starts tearing cities apart.
Jean Grey unleashes the Phoenix and burns him away.

k: A telepathic bodyguard with a blade of energy
st: Psylocke guards the mutant dealer Caliban, then joins Apocalypse as a Horseman.

k: A winged mutant cage fighter in East Berlin
st: Apocalypse gives the wounded Angel metal wings and makes him a Horseman.
He dies when the X-Men's jet crashes.

k: Ororo, a Cairo street thief who controls weather
st: Apocalypse makes Ororo his first Horseman and amplifies her powers.
She turns on Apocalypse and joins the X-Men.

k: An X-Man changed by a cosmic force in space
st: Jean absorbs a cosmic force during a space rescue, and her powers grow out of control.
She kills Mystique by accident and flees, hunted by the X-Men and Magneto.
She destroys Vuk in space and vanishes in a burst of fiery light.

k: Leader of the D'Bari, shape-shifting aliens
st: Vuk, leader of the shape-shifting D'Bari, manipulates Jean to steal the cosmic force inside her.
Jean takes the power back and destroys Vuk in space.

k: Cyborg security chief for Transigen
st: Pierce and his Reavers hunt Logan to take back Laura, a young mutant.
The children escaped from Transigen turn on him and kill him.

k: Transigen's head scientist
st: Rice runs Transigen's program that breeds mutant children as weapons.

k: A feral clone of Logan in his prime
st: X-24 kills Charles Xavier and the Munson family.
Laura kills him with an adamantium bullet to the head.

k: Francis, who runs a lab that turns people into mutants
st: Ajax tortures Wade Wilson to trigger his mutation, leaving him scarred.
He kidnaps Vanessa to lure Wade into a fight.

k: Ajax's super-strong right hand
st: Angel Dust helps Ajax run his lab and fights Colossus at the scrapyard.
Negasonic's blast knocks her out, and Colossus carries her from the wreck.

k: A cybernetic soldier from the future
st: Cable travels back in time to kill Russell before the boy becomes a killer.
He teams up with Deadpool and spends his last time jump saving Wade's life.

k: Russell, an angry young mutant who throws fire
st: Russell attacks the staff of his mutant orphanage and is locked in the Ice Box.
He frees Juggernaut and sets out to kill the orphanage's headmaster.
Moved by Deadpool's sacrifice, he spares the headmaster.

k: Head of a mutant re-education orphanage
st: The headmaster abuses the young mutants in his care.
Dopinder runs him over with his taxi.

k: An unstoppable mutant held in the Ice Box
st: Freed by Russell, Juggernaut tears Deadpool in half and joins the attack on the orphanage.
Colossus, Negasonic and Yukio defeat him at the orphanage.

k: A Juggernaut variant in Cassandra Nova's service
st: In the raid on Cassandra Nova's lair, X-23 kills Juggernaut, and the heroes take his helmet to block her telepathy.

k: A huge mutant in Cassandra Nova's service
st: Blob stands among Cassandra Nova's mutant forces in the Void.

k: The doctor running a hospital for young mutants
st: Dr. Reyes holds five young mutants in a hidden hospital for the Essex Corporation.
She moves to kill Dani Moonstar, and the Demon Bear kills her.

k: A monstrous bear stalking Dani Moonstar
st: The Demon Bear tears into the hospital and the young mutants inside.
Dani faces her fear and calms the bear, which comes from her own power.

k: A mutant master of magnetism fighting for mutantkind
st: Magneto attacks a missile base, and the X-Men stop him.
He builds Asteroid M as a haven for mutants, but his follower Fabian Cortez betrays him.
He joins forces with the X-Men against greater threats, including the Phalanx.
Xavier leaves the X-Men to Magneto, who stands trial for his past crimes.
After the Genosha massacre, he shuts down Earth's magnetic field to force humanity's hand.
As Asteroid M is stopped, he and several X-Men vanish in a flash of light.
Stranded in ancient Egypt, he saves a city from a black hole, and Apocalypse kills him.

k: Giant robots built to hunt mutants
st: Bolivar Trask's Sentinels hunt down mutants, and the X-Men strike back.
Master Mold, the Sentinel factory, turns on its makers and plots to rule humanity.
A giant Wild Sentinel slaughters the mutants of Genosha.
Prime Sentinels, humans fitted with machine parts, hunt mutants around the world.
When Jean puts Bastion's own collar on him, every Prime Sentinel shuts down.

k: The scientist behind the Sentinel program
st: Trask builds the Sentinels to round up mutants.

k: A geneticist obsessed with mutant DNA
st: Mister Sinister and his Nasty Boys battle the X-Men as he hunts mutant DNA.
He reveals that Madelyne Pryor is his clone of Jean Grey and turns her into the Goblin Queen.
Jean returns as the Phoenix and burns his stolen mutant DNA away, leaving him a powerless old man.

k: Cyclops's wife, who believes she is Jean Grey
st: Learning she is Sinister's clone of Jean, Madelyne becomes the Goblin Queen and attacks the X-Men.
She turns on Sinister and leaves to find her own path.

k: An ancient mutant who preaches survival of the fittest
st: In ancient Egypt, En Sabah Nur embraces his destiny as Apocalypse and kills Magneto.
Apocalypse gathers mutant Horsemen and schemes to rule a world of the strong.
He abducts the world's psychics to remake time, but the X-Men stop him at the Axis of Time.
In the year 3960, he rules the world and wants young Nathan Summers as his next body.
He raises Gambit from the dead as his Horseman, Death, and his mind ends up hiding inside Gambit.
Rogue pulls his essence out of Gambit and traps it in a gem that Cable keeps.

k: Wolverine's savage old enemy
st: Sabretooth stalks Wolverine and clashes with the X-Men again and again.
Xavier tries to reach his better nature, but Sabretooth turns on the X-Men.
He joins Wolverine's raid on a Weapon X lab overrun by the Brood and escapes alive.

k: A shape-shifter who can wear any face
st: Disguised as Gambit, Mystique tries to assassinate Senator Kelly.
In a mid-credits scene, Mystique is shown to have killed Valerie Cooper and taken her place.

k: Cain Marko, Xavier's unstoppable stepbrother
st: Juggernaut smashes his way through the X-Mansion hunting his stepbrother, Charles Xavier.

k: A Soviet super soldier with deadly metal coils
st: Revived from cold storage, Omega Red battles Wolverine and the X-Men.
Freed by accident in a Weapon X lab, he attacks Wolverine's team, and Wolverine beats him.

k: A ratings-mad tyrant from another dimension
st: Mojo pulls the X-Men into his dimension to fight for his TV ratings.
He traps Jubilee and Roberto inside a deadly video game.

k: A cosmic force bonded to Jean Grey
st: The Phoenix saves Jean from a shuttle crash in space and bonds with her.
Twisted by Mastermind and the Hellfire Club, it becomes Dark Phoenix and consumes a star.
On the Moon, the Phoenix and Jean part, and Jean survives.
The Phoenix rises in Jean again to stop Bastion and Mister Sinister, then fades away.

k: An illusion-casting member of the Hellfire Club
st: Mastermind uses illusions to pull Jean Grey into the Hellfire Club.

k: Leader of the anti-mutant Friends of Humanity
st: Graydon Creed leads the Friends of Humanity, a hate group that attacks mutants.
Kidnapped by the Acolytes, he is put on trial in the Savage Land until the X-Men get him out.
A news broadcast reports that he has been elected President of the United States.

k: A mutant follower of Magneto on Asteroid M
st: Cortez betrays Magneto and seizes control of Asteroid M.

k: Moira MacTaggert's reality-warping son
st: Proteus escapes Muir Island and bends reality as he hunts for his father.

k: A man with a burning hatred for mutants
st: Bastion is behind the Wild Sentinel that slaughters the mutants of Genosha.
He launches Operation: Zero Tolerance, sending Prime Sentinels after mutants.
Jean shuts down his Sentinels, and he seems to die trying to crash Asteroid M into Earth.

k: A time-traveling pharaoh with advanced weapons
st: Pharaoh Rama-Tut fires a giant beam weapon at En Sabah Nur and the stranded X-Men.
When Apocalypse opens a black hole over his city, he flees to the future in his Sphinx ship.

k: Gambit, raised from the dead as Apocalypse's Horseman
st: Apocalypse raises Gambit from the dead and makes him Death, one of his Horsemen.
As Death, he brainwashes Nightcrawler and kidnaps Rogue.
Rogue pulls Apocalypse out of him, and Gambit comes back to the X-Men.

k: Head of X-Factor, a government team of mutants
st: Valerie Cooper's X-Factor, with Havok and Polaris, hunts X-Force and captures Jubilee.
A mid-credits scene reveals that Mystique has killed the real Valerie Cooper.

k: A powerful mutant among the Acolytes
st: In the Savage Land, Exodus and the Acolytes put the kidnapped Graydon Creed on trial.
The standoff in the Savage Land ends with Exodus dead.

k: Abraham Kieros, a Horseman of Apocalypse
st: Cable's X-Force tracks down War and interrogates him about Apocalypse.

k: A telepath working with the government's X-Factor
st: Emma Frost tips off X-Force, then leads them into an ambush set by X-Factor.

k: The Danger Room's AI, come to life
st: The Danger Room's AI absorbs Polaris's power, takes an android body as Danger and locks down the mansion.
She hijacks a jet to confront Xavier on Genosha, and Xavier, Jean, Bishop and Polaris defeat her.

k: Insect-like aliens that grow inside living hosts
st: In a Weapon X lab, Dr. Cornelius turns into a Brood alien, and the lab burns the Brood as Wolverine's team escapes.

k: A billionaire and Reed Richards's rival
st: Victor Von Doom funds Reed's space mission and is changed by the same cosmic storm.
As his body turns to metal, he takes the name Doom and attacks the Fantastic Four.
Beaten by the Fantastic Four, he freezes solid in his metal form and is shipped to Latveria.
Revived by the Silver Surfer's energy, he steals the Surfer's board and its power.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Johnny Storm, carrying all four powers, knocks him off the board into the sea.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A cosmic herald who leaves craters across Earth
st: The Silver Surfer streaks around the globe, preparing Earth for his master.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
The U.S. military captures him and holds him in a cell.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
He turns on Galactus and saves Earth.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A vast cosmic cloud that devours worlds
op: The Silver Surfer and the Fantastic Four
st: Galactus arrives at Earth to consume it.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
The Silver Surfer flies into Galactus and destroys him in a blinding blast.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A U.S. general with a grudge against Reed
st: General Hager forces the Fantastic Four to work with Victor Von Doom to catch the Silver Surfer.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A young vampire who wants to rule humanity
st: Deacon Frost defies the vampire elders and plans to raise the blood god La Magra.
He kills the elders and becomes La Magra using Blade's blood.
Blade injects him with anticoagulant darts, and he bursts apart.

k: Frost's mocking vampire lieutenant
st: Quinn serves Frost and survives being burned and maimed by Blade.
Blade finally kills him at the Temple of Eternal Night.

k: Frost's lover and vampire enforcer
st: Mercury helps Frost hunt Blade and raise La Magra.
Blade kills her at the Temple of Eternal Night.

k: A pureblood vampire elder
st: Dragonetti tries to rein Frost in, and Frost leaves him to burn in the sunrise.

k: The first Reaper, a vampire-killing mutant
st: Nomak spreads the Reaper strain, a plague that feeds on vampires.
He kills his father, Damaskinos, for creating him.
Beaten by Blade, he drives Blade's sword into himself.

k: An ancient vampire overlord
st: Damaskinos asks Blade for help against the Reapers, hiding that he made them.

k: A brutal Bloodpack vampire who despises Blade
A vampire leader who frames Blade
st: Danica Talos awakens Dracula in the Syrian desert and frames Blade for killing a human.
Blade stabs Drake with the Daystar arrow, and the virus it releases kills her.

k: Danica's brother and fellow vampire leader
st: Asher stands with his sister Danica as her vampires hunt Blade and the Nightstalkers.
Abigail Whistler kills him in the assault on the Talos building.

k: Dracula, the first vampire, woken in the Syrian desert
st: Danica's vampires awaken Drake, the original vampire once known as Dracula.
Blade stabs him with the Daystar arrow, and the virus kills him.

k: A hulking vampire enforcer with metal teeth
st: Grimwood serves Danica as muscle, and Hannibal King kills him in the final assault.

k: A powerful vampire of the House of Chthon
st: Marcus turns Krista Starr into a vampire and makes her his agent.
He secretly plots against the pureblood vampires who lead his house.
With Blade's help, he unleashes a virus on the purebloods at their conclave, then faces Blade.

k: Wilson Fisk, a businessman secretly running crime
st: The Kingpin hires Bullseye to kill Nikolas Natchios and frame Daredevil.
Daredevil beats him but spares him, and the police arrest him.

k: An Irish assassin who never misses
st: Bullseye kills Nikolas Natchios with Daredevil's own weapon, then kills Elektra.
Daredevil throws him from a church, and he wakes in a guarded hospital bed, his aim still perfect.

k: An ancient order of mystic assassins
st: The Hand sends its deadliest killers to seize Abby Miller, a girl they call the Treasure.

k: The Hand's leading assassin
st: Kirigi leads the Hand's assassins in hunting Elektra and Abby.
Elektra kills him in the hedge maze of her childhood home.

k: A Hand assassin whose touch is poison
st: Typhoid's poisoned kiss nearly kills Elektra.
She dies in the final battle at Elektra's childhood home.

k: A Tampa crime boss and money launderer
st: After his son dies in a sting, Saint has Frank Castle's whole family murdered.
Frank turns Saint against those closest to him, then drags him to his death behind a car.

k: Howard Saint's wife
st: Livia demands that Frank Castle's entire family be killed.
Howard, tricked into believing she is having an affair with Quentin Glass, kills her.

k: Howard Saint's right-hand man
st: Glass runs the Saints' business and helps hunt Frank Castle.
Frank makes Howard believe Glass is sleeping with Livia, and Howard kills him.

k: Howard Saint's surviving son
st: John helps massacre Frank Castle's family, and Frank later kills him.

k: A giant hitman hired by Saint
st: The Russian nearly beats Frank to death in his apartment before Frank kills him.

k: A singing hitman from Memphis
st: Harry Heck hunts Frank for Saint, and Frank kills him in a car shootout.

k: An AI that won its war and took the Infinity Stones
st: Ultron wins his war, takes Vision's body and all six Infinity Stones, and wipes out life in his universe.
He discovers the Watcher and starts destroying universe after universe.
The Guardians upload Arnim Zola's mind into him, and Zola takes over Ultron's body.
Ultron returns, comes to see that peace needs the living, and helps Captain Carter reach the Watcher.
He draws the Watchers' fire so the others can escape, and he is destroyed.

k: A HYDRA scientist living as a computer mind
st: Zola's mind, stored in a computer, is fired into Ultron and takes over his body.
He fights Killmonger for the Infinity Stones until Strange Supreme traps them both in a pocket dimension.

k: Erik Stevens, a soldier who saves Tony Stark
st: Erik Stevens saves Tony Stark in Afghanistan and wins his trust.
He betrays Tony, kills T'Challa, and makes himself king of Wakanda.
Recruited by the Watcher, he turns on the Guardians to take the Infinity Stones.
Strange Supreme traps him with Zola in a pocket dimension.

k: A grieving Doctor Strange who breaks every rule
st: To save Christine Palmer, Strange absorbs countless beings and grows monstrously powerful.
His fight against fate destroys his whole universe.
He joins the Watcher's Guardians and guards the trapped Killmonger and Zola.
He feeds heroes and villains to a forge to rebuild his lost world.
Captain Carter frees him from his inner demon, and he sacrifices himself to the forge.

k: A cosmic hoarder of rare beings
st: Star-Lord T'Challa's crew raids the Collector's vault and turns his own cages on him.

k: A grieving scientist hunting Avengers candidates
st: Grieving Janet, Hank Pym shrinks down and kills Fury's Avengers candidates one by one.
Fury and Loki expose him and end his killing spree.

k: Thor's brother, here to avenge his death
st: Loki brings an Asgardian army to Earth to avenge Thor.
Once the killer is caught, Loki stays and rules Earth.

k: HYDRA's leader, obsessed with the Tesseract
st: Red Skull uses the Tesseract to open a portal and summon a monster from another world.

k: Earth's heroes turned flesh-eating zombies
st: A virus from the Quantum Realm turns the Avengers into zombies that overrun the world.

k: A zombified Scarlet Witch
st: Vision keeps the zombified Wanda at Camp Lehigh, feeding her the living.
Years later, as the Queen of the Dead, she commands the zombie hordes.
She defeats the survivors, takes the Infinity Stones' power from the Hulk, and traps Kamala in an illusion.

k: A zombified Thanos wielding the Infinity Gauntlet
st: Zombie Thanos waits in Wakanda, wearing an Infinity Gauntlet missing only the Mind Stone.
In Wakanda, T'Challa knocks him into the molten vibranium core, destroying them both.

k: A zombified Carol Danvers
st: A zombified Captain Marvel locks Ikaris in an endless battle and attacks Kamala Khan's group.

k: A zombified king of Talokan
st: Zombie Namor attacks the survivors, and Kamala destroys him with her bangle.

k: The Asgardian king, turned by Wanda
st: Zombified, Thor fights for the Queen of the Dead in her assault on the Infinity Hulk.

k: A Kree prisoner of the Nova Corps
st: Freed from prison by Nebula, Yon-Rogg betrays her and steals the code in her head for Ronan.
He turns on Nebula again in the final battle, and Korg kills him.

k: Irani Rael, leader of the Nova Corps
st: Nova Prime Irani Rael secretly plots with Ronan to hand Xandar over to him.
Exposed by Nebula, she tries to flee and falls to her death after a struggle with Nebula.

k: A Kree warlord set on taking Xandar
st: Ronan's Dark Aster closes in on Xandar to seize the planet.
Nebula turns Xandar's shield on his ship, and he dies when it is destroyed.

k: A boy with Celestial powers who falls to Earth
st: Trained by his father Ego, young Peter attacks Earth in 1988 with Celestial powers.
Peter turns on Ego, crushes his seedling and blasts his body apart.

k: A Celestial who sends his son to prepare Earth
op: Peter Quill and the Avengers of 1988
st: Ego raises young Peter and sends him to Earth in 1988 to prepare it for his expansion.
He comes to Earth himself, but Peter destroys his body, and Ego lives on as his planet, vowing revenge.

k: A disgraced weapons maker out for revenge
st: On Christmas Eve, Hammer raids Avengers Tower to steal a vial that will give him great power.
Happy Hogan, turned into a purple brute by Bruce Banner's blood, stops him with Darcy Lewis.

k: The ruler of Sakaar and host of its death race
st: The Grandmaster keeps the stranded Tony Stark on Sakaar and makes him race in his deadly Grand Prix.
In the chaos of the race, a melt stick turns him into a puddle, and Valkyrie takes over Sakaar.

k: A Red Room leader with a living weapon
st: Melina sends a brainwashed Steve Rogers in the Hydra Stomper armor to bring her Captain Carter.
Steve flies the Stomper into the Red Room, and Melina is caught in the blast.

k: A war machine piloted by a mystery soldier
st: The Hydra Stomper, piloted by a brainwashed Steve Rogers, attacks Captain Carter's allies.
Free of the Red Room's control, Steve flies the Stomper into its base, and his body is not found.

k: A conquistador hunting the Fountain of Youth
st: Gonzolo leads Spanish soldiers into Mohawk lands to claim the Fountain of Youth for Queen Isabella.
Kahhori returns with the people of the Sky World, defeats his conquistadors, and he dies in the battle.

k: The tyrant king of a 1602 England
st: Crowned after Hela vanishes, King Thor orders Captain Carter arrested and rules by force.
He hands Peggy the scepter holding the Time Stone so she can stop the rifts.

k: A gamma kaiju that spawns an army of monsters
op: The Hulk and the Mech Avengers
st: Bruce Banner's attempt to purge the Hulk with gamma radiation creates the Apex, a kaiju that spawns gamma monsters.
Years later it returns, and Banner's Hulk burns it to ash and absorbs its radiation.

k: A witch turned 1930s Hollywood star
st: Agatha becomes a movie star and gets Howard Stark to fund a film she plans to use for a ritual.
She plots to drain the Celestial buried inside Earth, but Kingo talks her out of it.

k: A ruler of a broken Earth with an Iron Legion
st: After the Emergence wrecks Earth, Quentin Beck rules with the Iron Legion, and Riri Williams leads rebels against him.
Helped by the Watcher, Riri finds her hope again and defeats him.

k: A masked outlaw ruling a ghost town in 1872
st: In 1872, Xu Xialing kills the original Hood and takes his dark powers for herself.
As the Hood, she rules a ghost town, and Kate Bishop hunts her for her family's deaths.
Shang-Chi refuses to fight his sister, and Kate Bishop kills her.

k: A Watcher who puts Uatu on trial
st: The Eminence puts the Watcher on trial for breaking his oath and moves to stop Captain Carter's team.
He merges with two other Watchers to erase Peggy's team, but her sacrifice strips him of his power.
